title: SASSA Grants for Caregivers — Grant-in-Aid, Child Support & More
description: Complete guide for caregivers in South Africa. Learn about the Grant-in-Aid, Child Support Grant, and other SASSA grants available to those caring for children, the elderly, or disabled family members.

seo.metaTitle: SASSA Grants for Caregivers — Grant-in-Aid, Child Support & More
seo.metaDescription: Complete guide to SASSA grants for caregivers in South Africa. Learn about Grant-in-Aid (R530/month), Child Support Grant (R530/month), and other grants for those caring for family members.

contentBlocks.text: If you are caring for a family member — whether a child, elderly parent, or disabled relative — you may qualify for several SASSA grants depending on your circumstances.
This guide is for anyone caring for a child, elderly person, or disabled family member who wants to understand what financial support is available.
Caring for a vulnerable family member is a significant responsibility. SASSA provides Grant-in-Aid and the Child Support Grant to help caregivers meet the needs of those they care for.

The Grant-in-Aid is an additional R530 per month paid on top of an existing grant (Older Person Grant or Disability Grant). It is for beneficiaries who require full-time care from another person. The caregiver does not receive this grant — it is paid to the person receiving care.
If you are the primary caregiver of a child under 18, you can apply for the Child Support Grant of R530 per month per child. This grant has a less strict means test than the SRD grant.

checklist: Must be a South African citizen or permanent resident
Must be the primary caregiver of the person needing care
Must have a valid South African ID
For Grant-in-Aid: the person you care for must already receive a SASSA grant
restrictions: Grant-in-Aid is paid to the grant recipient, not the caregiver directly
Child Support Grant is means-tested for the caregiver

faqs.question: Can I get paid as a caregiver for looking after my elderly parent?
faqs.answer: Not directly. Your parent may qualify for the Grant-in-Aid on top of their Older Person Grant, but it is paid to them. You cannot claim a salary for being a family caregiver.

faqs.question: Can I receive the Child Support Grant if I am not the biological parent?
faqs.answer: Yes. If you are the primary caregiver of the child and have a valid ID, you can apply for the Child Support Grant on behalf of the child.

faqs.question: Can I receive both Grant-in-Aid and Child Support Grant?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you meet the criteria for both. One grant would be for a child in your care, and Grant-in-Aid would be for an older person or disabled person you care for.
